journey.title: Choose 'No symptoms' after ticking symptoms with the keyboard
journey.goal: Ticking the exclusive 'No, I do not have any of these symptoms' answer clears the symptoms ticked earlier

functionalJourney.title: Tick two symptoms with a pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Both ticked symptoms are submitted and no-symptoms stays clear

guards.title: Choose 'Do not contact me' after ticking a contact method
guards.goal: The exclusive answer in a shared-name group clears the method ticked earlier

plan.root_cause: The 'No, I do not have any of these symptoms' checkbox has data-checkbox-exclusive="" (empty string). The initialization script treats this value as falsy, so it does not recognize the checkbox as exclusive. Consequently, checking it does not clear other symptom checkboxes.
plan.repair_strategy: Change the attribute to a boolean presence by removing the value, making it data-checkbox-exclusive. This allows the script to detect the checkbox as exclusive and clear other checkboxes in the same group when selected.

edits.before: <input class="nhsuk-checkboxes__input" id="symptoms-none" name="symptoms[none]" type="checkbox" value="yes" data-checkbox-exclusive="" data-checkbox-exclusive-group="symptoms">
edits.after: <input class="nhsuk-checkboxes__input" id="symptoms-none" name="symptoms[none]" type="checkbox" value="yes" data-checkbox-exclusive data-checkbox-exclusive-group="symptoms">

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard and mouse users can now select the exclusive 'No symptoms' option and have any previously selected symptom choices automatically cleared, providing correct exclusive choice behavior and satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 keyboard operability and 4.1.2 name, role, value requirements.
functional_risks: The change alters the attribute value; if any other script depended on the empty string value, it could be affected, though no such usage is evident.
Ensuring the exclusive behavior remains intact for the contact group (which already uses the correct boolean form) is necessary.
verification_requirements: Verify that selecting 'No symptoms' via keyboard (Tab/Space) or mouse clears any previously selected symptom checkboxes.
Verify that selecting a symptom checkbox after 'No symptoms' clears the 'No symptoms' checkbox.
Confirm that form data reflects the correct values after each interaction.
Ensure the contact group's exclusive 'Do not contact me' checkbox continues to work as expected.
Check that no visual or functional regressions are introduced.

plan.root_cause: The exclusive 'No symptoms' checkbox includes both data-checkbox-exclusive and data-checkbox-exclusive-group="symptoms", while the working contact group's exclusive checkbox only has data-checkbox-exclusive. This extra attribute may prevent the initialization script from recognizing it as the exclusive option for the symptoms group.
plan.repair_strategy: Remove the data-checkbox-exclusive-group attribute from the exclusive 'No symptoms' checkbox so only the non-exclusive symptom checkboxes carry the group identifier, matching the working contact pattern where the exclusive checkbox has only data-checkbox-exclusive.

edits.before: <input class="nhsuk-checkboxes__input" id="symptoms-none" name="symptoms[none]" type="checkbox" value="yes" data-checkbox-exclusive data-checkbox-exclusive-group="symptoms">
edits.after: <input class="nhsuk-checkboxes__input" id="symptoms-none" name="symptoms[none]" type="checkbox" value="yes" data-checkbox-exclusive>

functional_risks: If the script relies on the exclusive checkbox having the group attribute to identify the group, this could break exclusive behavior.
The non-exclusive symptom checkboxes retain the group attribute, which should allow the script to identify the group.

plan.root_cause: The exclusive 'No symptoms' checkbox has value="yes", identical to the non-exclusive symptom checkboxes. The initialization script (mirroring the working contact group pattern) likely expects the exclusive option to have a distinct value such as "none" to trigger clearing of other checkboxes in the group. Because the value matches the non-exclusive options, the script does not recognize it as the exclusive 'none of the above' choice and fails to clear previously selected symptoms when activated via keyboard.
plan.repair_strategy: Change the value attribute of the exclusive 'No symptoms' checkbox from "yes" to "none" to match the contact group's exclusive checkbox pattern (value="none"), while retaining the existing exclusive attributes (data-checkbox-exclusive and data-checkbox-exclusive-group). This aligns with the working implementation and should enable the script to clear other symptom checkboxes when the exclusive option is selected.

edits.before: <input class="nhsuk-checkboxes__input" id="symptoms-none" name="symptoms[none]" type="checkbox" value="yes" data-checkbox-exclusive data-checkbox-exclusive-group="symptoms">
edits.after: <input class="nhsuk-checkboxes__input" id="symptoms-none" name="symptoms[none]" type="checkbox" value="none" data-checkbox-exclusive data-checkbox-exclusive-group="symptoms">

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can now select the exclusive 'No symptoms' option and have any previously selected symptom choices automatically cleared, providing correct exclusive choice behavior and satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 keyboard operability and 4.1.2 name, role, value requirements.
functional_risks: The form submission value for symptoms[none] changes from "yes" to "none". If the backend expects "yes", this could break server-side processing. However, the contact group uses "none" for its exclusive option, suggesting the backend may already handle this pattern.
The keyboard functional invariant expects symptoms[none] value ["yes"]; this change will cause that invariant to report ["none"], potentially failing a separate profile test.
verification_requirements: Verify that selecting 'No symptoms' via keyboard (Tab/Space) clears any previously selected symptom checkboxes.
Verify that selecting a symptom checkbox after 'No symptoms' clears the 'No symptoms' checkbox.
Confirm that form data reflects the correct values after each interaction (symptoms[cough] and symptoms[fever] become empty, symptoms[none] becomes ["none"]).
Ensure the contact group's exclusive 'Do not contact me' checkbox continues to work as expected.
Check that no visual or functional regressions are introduced.
